id: title:eli-r-ph:reject a split that leaves the person with no distinct ids

review.posthog_relevance: Adds ownership and reachability checks to the person identity splitting workflow, preventing orphaned identities or complete identity loss.
review.reason: Adds a check before calling the explicit-split RPC to ensure the supplied main_distinct_id actually belongs to this person, raising ValueError if not. P1.F3.H1. Adds a check before fetching distinct IDs to ensure that after the split, at least one distinct ID remains on the person. P1.F3.H2.

observations.behavior: Adds a check before calling the explicit-split RPC to ensure the supplied main_distinct_id actually belongs to this person, raising ValueError if not.
observations.posthog_connection: This prevents a split request from using a distinct ID that does not belong to the person, which could leave the person unreachable or orphaned. The check uses the PersonHog client to fetch the person record and compare its ID. No actual split occurs if the check fails.

observations.behavior: Adds a check before fetching distinct IDs to ensure that after the split, at least one distinct ID remains on the person. It fetches one more ID than requested and checks if all returned IDs are already seen.
observations.posthog_connection: This prevents a split request from removing all distinct IDs, which would make the person unreachable. The check relies on the PersonHog client returning a bounded set of IDs; if all returned IDs are already accounted for, the split would leave none. No actual split occurs if the check fails.
